$comment: BC Transit's West Kootenay (Nelson, Castlegar, Trail, Rossland, the Slocan Valley, Nakusp, Kaslo, Salmo), Creston Valley and Revelstoke systems, one feed as on Vancouver Island (docs/DESIGN.md#regions-and-feeds). Published by BC Transit through Consat (tmix.se), an operator id per system (ids checked 2026-10-28 by downloading each). Every route is drawn; overrides: routes.json. Region: kootenays. Terms: https://www.bctransit.com/open-data/terms-of-use/ (identify BC Transit as the source; no use of its marks).
name: BC Transit (Kootenays and Revelstoke)

static.$comment: Consat exports one system per request, so fetch-gtfs merges the parts, each its own agency (packages/data/src/gtfs-merge.ts; Consat's ids are global across systems), over the dates every part covers. calendar_dates.txt only, shape_dist_traveled in metres, a daily export version (config/regions/kootenays/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #1).

realtime.$comment: No API key and no stated request limit. One request covers every system (the endpoints take several operatorIds). On 2026-10-28 17:26, West Kootenay's buses reported and at 17:39 Revelstoke's; Creston Valley's endpoint had none (config/regions/kootenays/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #3).
realtime.$poll: Guess, as for BC Transit's other feeds: positions every 30 s while buses run (05:00-24:00), every 60 s overnight; trip updates every 2 minutes, 5 overnight; alerts every 5 minutes, 15 overnight. About 3,460 requests a day; dailyCap is a safety net. OPEN-QUESTIONS #2.
realtime.$staleGraceS: Guesses for 30 s fixes, as for BC Transit's other feeds (OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).

display.$tripId: Consat trip ids begin with the journey id, as in BC Transit's other feeds.
display.$feedVersion: Versions begin with an export date and sequence number, before slash-separated export times.
